company_name: YSB Inc. (藥師幮股份有限公司)
overview: YSB Inc. operates China's leading digital B2B platform for the outside-of-hospital (retail/primary-care) pharmaceutical and healthcare market, connecting upstream pharmaceutical manufacturers/distributors with downstream buyers such as monomer pharmacies, chain pharmacies and primary healthcare institutions. The business runs on two engines — a commission-based Online Marketplace and a larger, lower-margin Self-operation (direct sale/distribution) business — supplemented by a fast-growing private-label ("Targeted Product Launch") line and smaller SaaS/digital-health offerings. YSB is headquartered in Guangzhou, listed on the HKEX (IPO 2024), and reports in RMB.

business_model.summary: YSB makes money in two structurally different ways: (1) Online Marketplace — a capital-light, high-margin (~83-84% gross margin) commission model charging upstream sellers ~3.3% of transaction value, funded partly by buyer coupon subsidies (~0.5% of GMV); and (2) Self-operation Business — a capital-intensive, low-margin (~7-8% gross margin) direct wholesale/distribution model where YSB buys pharmaceutical and healthcare products from manufacturers and resells to downstream pharmacies/clinics, recognizing full transaction value as revenue. Within Self-operation, a private-label/"Targeted Product Launch" sub-segment (branded and YSB's own-brand products, >1,200 SKUs) carries materially higher margins and is the primary driver of blended margin expansion. A supply-chain finance business (order financing for downstream buyers, funded with third-party financial institutions) and SaaS/subscription tools (CloudComm for sellers, ePalm/PHDS for buyers, Cloud Consultation SaaS, YSB eLearn) generate smaller recurring revenue and are used mainly to deepen platform stickiness.

revenue_streams.name: Self-operation Business (direct distribution incl. private label)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — downstream buyers are monomer pharmacies, pharmacy chain headquarters/stores, and primary healthcare institutions (clinics); upstream counterparties are pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors (11,000+ marketplace sellers, 12,000+ self-operation suppliers)
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Mainland China; registered buyers cover 98.9% of counties and 91.5% of towns nationwide, with continued penetration into lower-tier/grassroots markets

main_competitors: Alibaba Health (JD/Ali Health adjacent consumer platforms)
competitive_position.market_position: Largest independent digital B2B platform focused specifically on the outside-of-hospital pharmaceutical market in China, with a long operating history (founded pre-IPO, listed 2024) versus SOE distributors that have more recently built competing digital platforms

moat_factors.description: ~461,000 average monthly active buyers (MAB) and ~4.2-4.3 million average monthly SKUs create liquidity that is hard for new entrants to replicate quickly, especially in lower-tier markets

Self-built smart supply chain system achieves ~4-hour average order processing, 96-97%+ on-time delivery, and a negative cash conversion cycle (~-35 to -39 days), funding working capital from trade payables rather than external debt
Paying ratio (MPB/MAB) consistently ~94%, implying very high repeat/paying engagement among active buyers, and distribution reach to 376,000+ primary healthcare institution users

Private-label portfolio (1,200+ SKUs, Leyaoshi, Yuandian, etc.) carries materially higher gross margin than general self-operation and is difficult for pure distributors to replicate without brand investment
Digital traceability (Jinfang TCM standards), medical insurance integration across 100+ cities, and compliance systems create switching costs for risk-averse pharmacy/clinic customers

weaknesses: Thin and still-low overall net margins (~1.1% adjusted net profit margin in FY2025) leave little room for competitive price pressure
Self-operation (distribution) business is low-margin and asset/working-capital intensive, resembling a wholesaler more than a software platform
Online Marketplace — the highest-margin segment — is shrinking (revenue -1.7% FY2025, -13.3% H1 FY2026) as third-party sellers are squeezed by a broader pharmaceutical retail downturn
SOE distributors (Jointown, Shanghai Pharmaceuticals) and internet giants (JD, Alibaba Health) have substantially larger balance sheets and can subsidize competing B2B platforms

Buyer growth has decelerated sharply (active buyer growth ~18% FY2024 → ~6.5% FY2025 → roughly flat in H1 FY2026), suggesting the core addressable market of registered/reachable pharmacies may be approaching saturation

growth_drivers: Private-label ("Go Upstream") strategy — own-brand transaction value grew ~283% in FY2025 and ~30% in H1 FY2026, lifting blended gross margin as mix shifts toward higher-margin SKUs
Targeted Product Launch Business (brand partnerships + private label) — transaction amounts up 111% in FY2025 and 18.6% in H1 FY2026, a structurally higher-margin growth engine within Self-operation

M&A — acquisition of Yikuai Pharmaceutical (Folding Space (Cayman) Ltd) met its FY2025 earn-out performance targets and is viewed as a template for further bolt-on consolidation of distribution/channel assets

On-demand pharmaceutical retail (new initiative, H1 FY2026) — "internal incubation + external investment" push into instant/C-end-adjacent medication delivery, a new growth vector beyond the core B2B model

AI/digital infrastructure — AI Operations Expert, AI Procurement, AI Smart Customer Service, and AI-assisted prescription review embedded into Cloud Consultation SaaS, aimed at supply chain cost reduction and higher-margin SaaS monetization

TCM (Traditional Chinese Medicine) decoction pieces standardization ("Jinfang standards") — volume +32.8% FY2025, +10% H1 FY2026, capturing a structural shift from "experience-based" to "data-driven" sourcing

Deepening penetration into lower-tier/grassroots markets and primary healthcare institutions (376,000+ institution users, +50,000 in FY2025) as China's "Healthy China 2030" and primary-care policy push continues

Supply chain financial services (order financing) — cumulative lending to downstream buyers grew double digits, increasing platform stickiness among chain pharmacy customers (MPB penetration ~75% of chain HQ users nationwide)

business.description: Average MAB growth fell from ~18% (FY2024) to ~6.5% (FY2025) to roughly flat (~460k, H1 FY2026), indicating the core platform may be nearing penetration limits in its addressable base of registered pharmacies/clinics
The company's highest-margin segment (~83% gross margin) saw revenue fall -1.7% in FY2025 and -13.3% in H1 FY2026 as a broader pharmaceutical retail downturn hit third-party sellers
General Self-operation gross margin is only ~7-8%; the business resembles a low-margin wholesale distributor outside of the private-label mix-shift

business.risk: Intensifying competition from SOE distributors and internet platforms
business.description: Jointown, Shanghai Pharmaceuticals and JD/Alibaba Health-adjacent platforms are building competing B2B digital channels, pressuring commission rates and buyer acquisition costs

business.risk: Customer concentration in a fragmented, price-sensitive market
business.description: Downstream customer base (monomer pharmacies, small chains, primary clinics) is price-sensitive and has limited switching costs for commoditized generic products

financial.description: FY2025 adjusted net profit margin was only ~1.1% (RMB237m on RMB21bn revenue); IFRS net profit was RMB146m — small buffers against margin compression or a revenue slowdown
Gearing ratio increased from 0.9% (FY2024) to 6.4% (FY2025) due to bank borrowings from discounted notes tied to the Yikuai Pharmaceutical acquisition

Cash and cash equivalents fell 31.8% in FY2025 (RMB1,041m → RMB710m), driven by increased placement into restricted deposits/time deposits/financial assets, though operating cash flow remained a net inflow
Further consideration shares were issued in March 2026 (490,000 shares at HK$12) tied to Yikuai Pharmaceutical's 2025 earn-out, a continuing dilution source as acquisition milestones are met

regulatory.description: The business operates squarely within PRC drug distribution, retail and e-commerce regulation (GSP/GMP-style compliance, medical insurance integration); policy shifts such as the "Guideline to Advance High-quality Development of Pharmaceutical Retail Industry" directly reshape industry economics

Order financing products for downstream buyers (RMB9.1bn cumulative lending FY2025) expose the company to evolving PRC fintech/consumer-lending oversight even though facilities are structured as purchase-restricted

Medical insurance system integration across 100+ cities and AI-assisted diagnosis/prescription tools (ClouWiseDoctor, Cloud Consultation) carry data-privacy and medical-practice compliance exposure as PRC health-data rules evolve

macro.description: Management repeatedly cites a "downturn in the pharmaceutical retail market" and "sluggish recovery and weak growth momentum" as the explicit cause of Online Marketplace revenue declines and buyer growth deceleration through FY2025 and H1 FY2026
Downstream pharmacy and clinic purchasing volumes are correlated with broader PRC consumer health spending and macro conditions

macro.risk: Interest rate sensitivity on treasury income
macro.description: Other income fell in FY2025 partly due to declining interest income on bank deposits/financial assets as PRC interest rates declined

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's outside-of-hospital pharmaceutical and healthcare market is in a structural transition from 'demand expansion' to 'value upgrading,' driven by an aging population, rising chronic disease management needs, the 'Healthy China 2030' policy framework, and continued digitalization of primary healthcare; near-term, the pharmaceutical retail sub-segment has been in a cyclical downturn pressuring smaller/independent pharmacies
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — healthcare/pharmaceutical demand is relatively defensive versus discretionary retail, but the specific sub-segment YSB serves (independent/chain retail pharmacies, primary clinics) has shown clear cyclical softness in 2025-2026 tied to broader PRC consumer and retail conditions
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct exposure; modest indirect effect through other income (interest on deposits/financial assets) and discounted-note finance costs
key_input_costs: Pharmaceutical and healthcare product procurement costs (COGS, the dominant cost line in Self-operation)
Labor (business development team of ~2,600-2,700 field staff)

recent_developments.event: Stock trading near 52-week lows (~HK$3.0-4.0 range vs. 52-week high ~HK$12.66), roughly -70% over the trailing year, reflecting market concern over decelerating buyer growth and the pharmaceutical retail downturn

H1 FY2026 interim results: revenue +4.5% YoY to RMB10,283m, gross margin flat at 11.2%, net profit attributable to owners +41.9% to RMB110.8m; MAB flat at ~460,000 and MPB ~430,000, both essentially unchanged YoY, confirming the growth deceleration flagged after FY2025
Share price fell sharply (reported single-day drop of as much as ~46% around lock-up related selling pressure following the 2024 IPO), contributing to the steep 52-week decline

FY2025 annual results released (23 March 2026): revenue +17.1% to RMB20,969.7m, gross profit +27.2%, adjusted net profit +51.2% to RMB237.1m; disclosed active buyer growth decelerating to 6.5% YoY (from ~18% in FY2024) and gearing ratio rising to 6.4% (from 0.9%) on acquisition-related bank borrowings

Completion of Yikuai Pharmaceutical (Folding Space (Cayman) Ltd) earn-out: 490,000 consideration shares issued at HK$12/share (23 March 2026) after Yikuai met its FY2025 revenue growth and net profit performance targets; 2,533,700 award shares granted to employees (10 February 2026)
Board announced/executed a voluntary share repurchase plan (reported up to HK$100 million), stating the board views the prevailing share price as undervaluing the company

Private-label (own-brand) transaction value grew ~283% YoY to RMB1,937m and Targeted Product Launch Business transaction value grew 111% to RMB2,445m, becoming the primary margin-expansion driver even as topline buyer growth slowed

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (2026-08) / FY2025 Annual Report (2026-03)

items.target: No explicit numeric guidance disclosed; management commentary frames MAB/MPB stability (~94% paying ratio, ~29 orders/paying buyer/month) as the near-term target rather than renewed high growth
items.notes: Management explicitly attributes flat buyer metrics to a 'sluggish recovery and weak growth momentum in the pharmaceutical retail market' rather than company-specific execution issues

items.metric: Private label / Targeted Product Launch growth
items.target: Continued high-speed growth of private label and Targeted Product Launch transaction value (no specific percentage target given)
items.notes: H1 FY2026 private label transaction value grew 30.4% YoY to RMB1,111m and Targeted Product Launch overall grew 18.6% to RMB1,281m; management reiterates this as the core margin/profit growth engine

items.target: Continued gradual gross margin improvement via own-brand/private-label mix shift; no specific percentage target disclosed
items.notes: Gross margin improved from 10.1% (FY2024) to 11.0% (FY2025) and held flat at 11.2% in H1 FY2026 vs H1 FY2025; management frames further improvement as mix-driven, not guided numerically

items.metric: New growth initiative: on-demand pharmaceutical retail
items.target: Qualitative commitment to scale a 'self-operated benchmark stores + ecosystem cooperation network' and 'front warehouse + traffic platform' model; no revenue or unit targets disclosed
items.notes: First substantively discussed in the H1 FY2026 interim report as a new growth vector via internal incubation plus external investment

items.target: Continuation of share repurchase program and dividend policy (FY2025 DPS RMB0.110 vs RMB0.075 FY2024, +46.7%)
items.notes: Board has signaled confidence via buybacks despite depressed share price; no explicit forward dividend or buyback size guidance for FY2026 found in filings reviewed

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman and CEO Zhang Buzhen's FY2025 letter frames 2026 priorities around 'strategic prudence + proactive advancement,' continuing dual engines of Online Marketplace and Self-operation, deepening the private-label/Go Upstream strategy, expanding AI across the supply chain, and pursuing further M&A/industrial chain investment while maintaining healthy financial conditions. The H1 FY2026 outlook section reiterates these themes and explicitly frames the on-demand pharmaceutical retail push as a new growth engine to offset maturing core-platform growth.

bull_case: Private-label and Targeted Product Launch businesses are growing very fast (111% and 283% respectively in FY2025) off a low base and carry structurally higher margins, giving a credible path to margin expansion even if buyer growth stays flat

Negative cash conversion cycle (~-35 to -39 days) and consistent operating cash inflow mean the core distribution model is self-funding and does not require external capital to grow, unlike many loss-making China platform IPOs

Deep structural tailwinds from China's aging population, primary healthcare policy push ('Healthy China 2030') and continued digitalization of a highly fragmented pharmaceutical retail/distribution chain support a multi-year addressable market expansion story

Stock has fallen roughly 70% over the trailing year to levels management itself has called undervalued (backed by an active buyback), creating a potential value entry point if buyer growth and margins stabilize

Diversification beyond the core platform — AI-enabled SaaS tools, supply chain financing, on-demand retail — gives multiple unproven but optionality-rich growth vectors beyond the maturing core marketplace
bear_case: Active buyer growth has collapsed from ~18% (FY2024) to ~6.5% (FY2025) to roughly flat (H1 FY2026), suggesting the core two-sided marketplace may already be near saturation in its addressable pharmacy/clinic base

The highest-margin segment (Online Marketplace, ~83% gross margin) is shrinking in absolute revenue terms (-13.3% YoY in H1 FY2026), while the business increasingly resembles a thin-margin pharmaceutical wholesaler (Self-operation gross margin only ~7-8%)

Absolute profitability remains very thin (FY2025 adjusted net margin ~1.1%), leaving little cushion if the broader China pharmaceutical retail downturn persists or competition compresses commission/distribution margins further

Rising competitive intensity from well-capitalized SOE distributors (Jointown, Shanghai Pharmaceuticals) and internet healthcare giants (JD Health, Alibaba Health) building competing B2B platforms threatens both buyer acquisition costs and commission economics

Severe share price decline (~70% over the trailing year, including a reported ~46% single-day drop around lock-up expiry) signals the market has lost confidence in the growth narrative, and continued earn-out share issuance (Yikuai Pharmaceutical) adds ongoing dilution
